subtitle: How a village notebook shook an empire

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of Gandhi standing amid indigo fields under a harsh sun
panels.action: Mahatma Gandhi stands barefoot at the edge of a vast indigo field in Champaran, his simple figure set against rows of blue-green plants and the looming silhouettes of planter bungalows in the distance.

dialogue.text: Champaran, 1917: a quiet lawyer with a notebook walked into the indigo fields—and forced the Raj to record its own injustice.

i18n.hi: चंपारण, 1917: एक शांत वकील डायरी लेकर नील की खेती में उतरा—और राज से उसकी ही ज्यादती लिखवा ली।

panels.shot: intimate mid-shot inside a Calcutta gathering, slightly low angle on Gandhi
panels.action: In a crowded Calcutta hall, Mahatma Gandhi sits on a simple chair, listening intently as peasants, lawyers and leaders swirl around him, his eyes calm yet curious.

dialogue.text: Before Champaran, Gandhi was still a newcomer in Indian politics, better known for South Africa than for any village in Bihar.

i18n.hi: चंपारण से पहले, गांधी भारतीय राजनीति में नए थे, दक्षिण अफ्रीका के ज्यादा, बिहार के किसी गाँव के कम जाने जाते थे।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Gandhi’s hands as a determined peasant grips them
panels.action: A weathered peasant hand, belonging to Raj Kumar Shukla, clasps Gandhi’s palm with stubborn urgency in a dim corner of the hall.

dialogue.text: There, a persistent indigo cultivator, Raj Kumar Shukla, seized his hand and refused to let go until he promised to see Champaran.

i18n.hi: वहीं, जिद्दी नील किसान राजकुमार शुक्ल ने उनका हाथ थाम लिया, और वचन लिए बिना छोड़ने से इनकार कर दिया।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder shot of Gandhi looking out from a train compartment
panels.action: Gandhi leans at the window of a slow train, watching flat Bihar plains roll past, bullock carts and thatched roofs slipping by under a hazy sky.

dialogue.speaker: mahatma_gandhi
dialogue.text: I must see with my own eyes before I speak.

i18n.hi: जब तक खुद न देखूँ, मुँह नहीं खोलूँगा।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of a Champaran village, slightly elevated
panels.action: Gandhi walks into a Champaran village lane, flanked by mud huts, lean cattle and wary peasants watching him from doorways.

dialogue.text: Champaran was not a battlefield, but a quiet countryside locked in a harsh contract called tinkathia—three kathas of every bigha forced under indigo.

i18n.hi: चंपारण कोई रणभूमि नहीं, शांत देहात था, जिसे एक सख्त करार ने बाँध रखा था—टिनकठिया, हर बीघा की तीन कठ्ठा ज़बरन नील।

panels.shot: mid-shot inside a poor peasant hut, candlelit, Gandhi seated on the floor
panels.action: Inside a smoky hut, Gandhi sits cross-legged, notebook on his knee, as a gaunt peasant couple speaks, the woman clutching a hungry child.

dialogue.text: Tenant after tenant spoke of leases they could not read, of forced indigo, of low returns and heavy illegal exactions when they tried to escape.

i18n.hi: एक-एक मज़दूर ने अनपढ़ पट्टों, जबरन नील, घटिया दाम और भागने की कोशिश पर भारी गैरकानूनी वसूली की कहानी सुनाई।

panels.shot: close-up on Gandhi’s notebook and face, lit by a small lamp
panels.action: Gandhi bends over a worn notebook, his handwriting neat and steady as he records a peasant’s statement beside the flicker of a small oil lamp.

dialogue.text: Gandhi did not call for revolt. He opened a notebook. He wrote names, rents, beatings, dates—turning whispered misery into a record.

i18n.hi: गांधी ने बगावत नहीं बुलवाई, उन्होंने कॉपी खोली। नाम, लगान, मार, तारीखें लिखीं—फुसफुसाती पीड़ा को दर्ज कर दिया।

panels.shot: formal mid-shot in a colonial office, slight low angle on a magistrate facing Gandhi
panels.action: In the Motihari courthouse, a British magistrate sits stiff behind a desk while Gandhi stands calmly before him, hands lightly clasped.

dialogue.text: The district authorities ordered him to leave Champaran. Gandhi read the order, reflected, and quietly wrote his reply.

i18n.hi: जिला अफसरों ने उन्हें चंपारण छोड़ने का हुक्म दिया। गांधी ने आदेश पढ़ा, सोचा, और चुपचाप जवाब लिख दिया।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Gandhi standing outside the court, surrounded by peasants and lawyers
panels.action: Outside the courthouse, Gandhi addresses a ring of anxious peasants and local lawyers, his slight frame steady amid the crowd.

dialogue.speaker: mahatma_gandhi
dialogue.text: I obey the law of conscience. I will not leave Champaran.

i18n.hi: मैं अंतरात्मा का कानून मानता हूँ। मैं चंपारण नहीं छोड़ूँगा।

panels.shot: wide shot inside the courtroom packed with peasants, lawyers in front rows
panels.action: The Motihari courtroom is packed with barefoot peasants pressing at the door, while Gandhi stands in the dock, lawyers like Rajendra Prasad seated nearby.

dialogue.text: The magistrate, faced with a nonviolent refusal and an unexpected crowd, postponed sentence. Gandhi’s quiet defiance forced the government to rethink its own order.

i18n.hi: मजिस्ट्रेट ने अहिंसक इंकार और अनपेक्षित भीड़ देख सज़ा टाल दी। गांधी की शांत अवज्ञा ने सरकार को अपना हुक्म दोबारा सोचने पर मजबूर किया।

panels.shot: group mid-shot of Gandhi with Indian lawyers in a verandah meeting
panels.action: On a shaded verandah, Gandhi sits with Rajendra Prasad and other local lawyers, their papers spread on a mat as they listen to him intently.

dialogue.text: He turned to the lawyers of Bihar, asking them not just to argue in court, but to live among the peasants and share the risk of disobeying.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने बिहार के वकीलों से कहा, सिर्फ अदालत में बहस नहीं, किसानों के बीच रहकर अवज्ञा का जोखिम भी बाँटिए।

panels.shot: dynamic montage-like wide shot of multiple huts with Gandhi’s team taking statements
panels.action: Across several village courtyards, Gandhi’s co-workers—lawyers and volunteers—sit with peasants, each scene showing someone writing as villagers speak.

dialogue.text: Over weeks, they gathered hundreds of statements. Each was a story of rent, coercion, beatings; together they became evidence no file could ignore.

i18n.hi: हफ्तों में सैकड़ों बयान जुटे। हर एक में लगान, दबाव, मारपीट की दास्तान; सब मिलकर ऐसा सबूत बने जिन्हें कोई फाइल अनदेखा न कर सकी।

panels.shot: interior shot of a planter’s bungalow verandah, planter and Gandhi seated opposite
panels.action: On the verandah of a large planter’s bungalow, a European indigo planter sits rigid in a cane chair as Gandhi sits opposite on a plain stool, listening more than speaking.

dialogue.text: He also met the planters, neither flattering nor provoking, asking them to explain tinkathia and their claims, and quietly comparing their words with the villagers’ accounts.

i18n.hi: उन्होंने साहूकारों से भी मिले, न खुशामद की, न उकसाया; टिनकठिया और अपने हक समझाने को कहा, और चुपचाप उनकी बातें किसानों की गवाही से मिलाईं।

panels.shot: mid-shot of Gandhi writing a letter at a simple desk, lantern beside him
panels.action: Late at night, Gandhi sits at a simple desk in a modest lodging, drafting a letter, stacks of recorded testimonies beside him.

dialogue.text: By now, the government knew he had not stirred a riot, but an inquiry. The Lieutenant-Governor’s council decided to appoint an official committee.

i18n.hi: अब तक सरकार को दिख गया कि उन्होंने दंगा नहीं, जाँच खड़ी की है। लेफ्टिनेंट-गवर्नर की काउंसिल ने आधिकारिक कमेटी बनाने का फैसला किया।

panels.shot: formal group wide shot of the Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee in session
panels.action: In a formal hall, the Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee sits at a long table—British officials, European planters and Gandhi among the Indian members, papers neatly arranged.

dialogue.text: In 1917, the Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee began its work. Gandhi, now inside the machinery of the Raj, laid out the peasants’ testimony as disciplined fact.

i18n.hi: 1917 में चंपारण एग्रेरियन इन्क्वायरी कमेटी बनी। गांधी, अब राज की मशीनरी के भीतर, किसानों की गवाही को सधे हुए सबूत की तरह रख रहे थे।

panels.shot: close-up of Gandhi speaking calmly in the committee, others listening
panels.action: Gandhi leans slightly forward at the committee table, speaking in an even tone, while a British member and a planter listen, pens poised.

dialogue.speaker: mahatma_gandhi
dialogue.text: We do not ask for favour. We ask that what is written be believed.

i18n.hi: हम रहम नहीं माँगते, बस चाहते हैं जो लिखा है, उस पर भरोसा हो।

panels.shot: medium shot of a British official reading aloud from the committee report draft
panels.action: A British official member reads from a draft report, spectacles low on his nose, other members following the text.

dialogue.text: The official report acknowledged planter abuses and recommended partial refund of illegal exactions, and the gradual ending of the tinkathia system.

i18n.hi: सरकारी रिपोर्ट ने साहूकारों की ज्यादती मानी, गैरकानूनी वसूली का हिस्सा लौटाने और टिनकठिया धीरे-धीरे खत्म करने की सिफ़ारिश की।

panels.shot: wide shot of a village gathering as a volunteer explains the settlement to peasants
panels.action: Under a banyan tree, Gandhi stands with local leaders, explaining the settlement terms to a circle of peasants, some hopeful, some uncertain.

dialogue.text: This was no instant miracle. Planters resisted, and withdrawal from indigo took time. Yet for the first time, the system itself had been condemned by the state’s own pen.

i18n.hi: ये कोई पलभर का चमत्कार नहीं था। साहूकार अड़े रहे, नील छोड़ने में वक़्त लगा। पर पहली बार, उसी राजकलम ने इस सिस्टम को कटघरे में खड़ा किया।

panels.shot: intimate mid-shot of Gandhi starting a village school with children around
panels.action: Gandhi sits on the ground teaching letters to a small group of village children, with a volunteer writing on a rough board, mothers watching from behind.

dialogue.text: Even as reforms moved slowly, Gandhi stayed to start schools, clean villages and build habits of self-respect that would outlast any one settlement.

i18n.hi: इधर सुधार धीमे चले, उधर गांधी रुके रहे—स्कूल खोले, गाँव साफ़ कराए, और आत्मसम्मान की आदतें डालीं जो किसी एक समझौते से लंबी चलें।

panels.shot: quiet close-up of Gandhi closing his notebook, soft light on his face
panels.action: Sitting alone on a charpoy in the fading light, Gandhi gently closes the now well-worn notebook of testimonies, his face thoughtful and composed.

dialogue.text: Champaran became Gandhi’s first great satyagraha in India—a struggle not of slogans but of patient documentation, disciplined refusal and negotiated reform.

i18n.hi: चंपारण, गांधी का भारत में पहला बड़ा सत्याग्रह बना—नारे नहीं, धैर्य से दस्तावेज़ीकरण, सधे इंकार और समझौतावादी सुधार की लड़ाई।

panels.shot: epic high wide shot of the Champaran landscape with distant peasants at work
panels.action: From high above, the Champaran countryside stretches out, peasants working in fields no longer bound by indigo rows, Gandhi’s small figure walking a dusty path.

dialogue.text: In Champaran, truth did not shout; it was written, signed and read into the record—and in that quiet act, a village’s suffering began to bend an empire’s law.

i18n.hi: चंपारण में सच ने शोर नहीं मचाया; वह लिखा गया, हस्ताक्षर हुआ, रिकॉर्ड में पढ़ा गया—और उसी शांत क़दम से, एक गाँव का दुःख साम्राज्य के कानून को मोड़ने लगा।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a village notebook shook an empire
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक गाँव की कॉपी ने साम्राज्य हिला दिया
